title: Quality Management Microservice

_meta.purpose: Machine-readable PRD for the Quality Management Microservice (quality-inspection-and-notification) flat single-concern microservice foundation; metadata-only scope with explicit non-claims.

goals.scalability: Independent horizontal scaling per ADR-0348 (autosharding/auto-rebalance); tenant- and cell-scoped writes with no shared mutable global state. Foundation scope: metadata-only, no measured scaling evidence.
goals.security: Default-deny tenant isolation via Cedar (ADR-0243) and tenant-as-scope (ADR-0244); no raw credential/PII/secret bytes in the domain. Foundation scope: no runtime authentication.
goals.performance: Per-manifest SLO and capacity targets (ADR-0340) required before any GA claim; async-first eventing on Pulsar. Foundation scope: no measured SLO.
goals.efficiency: FinOps cost attribution (ADR-0344) and flat single-concern crates (ADR-0131/0132) that avoid platform bloat. Foundation scope: no runtime cost telemetry.
goals.reliability: Idempotent metadata operations and rollback-first promotion. Foundation scope: no DR drill evidence.

non_goals: No live quality-inspection runtime, inventory blocking/release mutation, laboratory instrument integration, PDF generation, email delivery, supplier network, CAPA workflow engine, or regulatory e-signature runtime.
No durable persistence, warehouse mutation, manufacturing execution, procurement supplier calls, plant-maintenance notification, Workflow execution, runtime audit-chain emission, or cloud deployment.
No SAP, Oracle, or Dynamics quality-management exhaustive parity claim.

acceptance_criteria.given: a material has defined inspection characteristics, sampling, AQL, effective date, source refs, and approval evidence
acceptance_criteria.when: the quality-management domain approves the inspection plan
acceptance_criteria.then: tenant, legal entity, plant, item, plan type, characteristic count, sample size, AQL basis points, effective date, source refs, approval evidence, idempotency key, state, schema version, and false inspection-runtime/inventory-mutation/Workflow/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: an approved inspection plan exists and an inspection lot has accepted/rejected result quantities
acceptance_criteria.then: inspection lot, plan, tenant, legal entity, plant, item, batch, source refs, result evidence, inspected/accepted/rejected quantities, defect count, AQL, max rejected quantity, pass/fail decision, certificate-allowed flag, notification-required flag, and false inventory/Workflow/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: a usage decision was made and the inspection passed
acceptance_criteria.then: certificate, inspection lot, tenant, legal entity, plant, item, batch, customer, result count, certificate profile, evidence, idempotency key, ready-for-output flag, and false PDF/email/outbound-delivery/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: an inspection lot fails its acceptance threshold
acceptance_criteria.then: notification, inspection lot, tenant, legal entity, plant, item, severity, defect count, corrective-action due days, defect source, evidence, idempotency key, corrective-action-required flag, and false CAPA Workflow/supplier-network/maintenance/cloud flags are present

acceptance_criteria.given: untrusted identifiers, source refs, evidence refs, dates, limits, quantities, or overclaim flags enter the quality-management domain
acceptance_criteria.then: prefix-only, traversal, whitespace/control, credential-shaped refs, invalid dates, invalid AQL, inconsistent inspection totals, missing plan approval, missing usage decision, certificate on rejected inspection, notification on accepted inspection, and invalid corrective-action due days are refused

decision_log.decision: Quality Management enters the enterprise microservice set as a flat quality-inspection-and-notification domain crate rather than a monolithic ERP/QM module; SAP QM and broader ERP quality coverage is mapped through Tenant RBAC parity composition while inspection execution runtime, inventory mutation, certificate rendering, CAPA Workflow execution, supplier collaboration, runtime audit emission, and cloud deployment remain explicit non-claims.
